He said the tilt toward foreign stocks is due to high U.S. valuations. His JD exposure includes call options that expire as late as 2029, which shows he is prepared to wait a long time. On Wednesday, the NASDAQ Composite went down as much as 4.64% intraday before it closed down 0.62%, which shows how volatile the market Burry is investing in has become.

He calls the long tilt temporary "because I am continuing to assess short opportunities." The only bearish options he still holds are puts on a software stock and a life insurer. He has also sold the final half of his NASDAQ index puts.

He said puts have become "very expensive" as the VIX rises. That leaves shorting common stock as his main bearish tool, a trade he called "asymmetric the wrong way."

Michael Burry said about 25% of his portfolio is in cash. Most of it came from winning puts plus new money, and he is working to invest it.

Key Takeaways

Morgan Stanley cut its MercadoLibre price target to $2,350 from $2,450 on Nov. 23 and kept its Overweight rating, leaving the target 66% above the stock.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue rose 45%, but operating income fell 6% as it spent more on free shipping, warehouse space and marketing in Brazil.

On 2028 earnings estimates, $2,350 is 32x, far below the stock's five-year average of 61x, so the target doesn't need a higher multiple.

Analysts have cut those 2028 estimates since the third-quarter report, and Sea's Shopee keeps pushing in Brazil. Until margins recover, $2,350 looks like a best case.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) has lost 40% since its late-January high, and Morgan Stanley just cut its price target for the third time since March. Analyst Andrew Ruben kept his Overweight rating on Nov. 23, and his new $2,350 target sits 66% above the stock.

Record growth, thinner margins

On Nov. 4, MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion. But operating income fell 6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin, and GAAP EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 analysts expected. The company blamed more free shipping, warehouse space added ahead of the holiday peak and heavier affiliate marketing in Brazil.

And MercadoLibre has competition in Brazil. Sea Limited (SE:NYSE) said Brazil was again Shopee's fastest-growing market in the third quarter. Shopee's adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $269.2 million across all its markets, so Sea has the profit to keep pushing.

"Today, as tech stocks were weak, I sold the rest (final half) of the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) put position," said Burry.

His only outstanding bearish options positions are tied to Palantir Technologies (PLTR) and MetLife (MET). Burry added that he is still evaluating potential short opportunities but currently prefers owning stocks. Around 25% of his portfolio is held in cash.

Overseas Stocks Lead Burry's Biggest Positions

Nvidia Short Could Return Near $200

Burry said he continues to hold call options on Nvidia, which have already doubled in value. "My plan is to short Nvidia again nearer $200/share during a period of market optimism. That time is not now."

MercadoLibre reported strong e-commerce and fintech activity in Latin America, with revenue rising 45% year over year and gross merchandise volume in Argentina up 40%, while operating income declined 6% as shipping, logistics, marketing, and credit costs weighed on short term profitability.

Management is leaning into free shipping for MELI+ members and rapid expansion of the Mercado Pago credit book. These choices support user engagement and payment volume but also bring higher funding needs and rising late loans that keep margins and cash generation under pressure.

We will now look at how MercadoLibre's heavier logistics and shipping reinvestment shapes the investment narrative that previously focused on cash flow.

Scan how MercadoLibre's reinvestment story compares with other platforms leaning into growth over near term profits by reviewing our curated list of 37 high quality undervalued stocks.

MercadoLibre Investment Narrative Recap

For a shareholder in MercadoLibre, the core belief is that heavy spending on logistics, shipping and the Mercado Pago credit book eventually supports a larger, more entrenched platform across Latin America. According to John_Eric, an investor in the Simply Wall St Community who wrote the Narrative, the key short term catalyst is whether adjusted free cash flow moves back into positive territory.

Recent results, with revenue up 45% but operating income down 6%, keep that cash flow question front and center. Rising late loans add to the near term risk that the credit portfolio consumes more funding without an offsetting earnings recovery, so the upcoming quarters around Q4 remain important for testing the reinvestment thesis.

The most relevant recent development is MercadoLibre leaning harder into free shipping for MELI+ and logistics capacity ahead of the holiday period. Management expects limited margin impact, but investors are already seeing lower net profit margins at 4.9% compared with 7.9% last year, so there is limited room for execution missteps on costs.

This same announcement interacts directly with the main catalysts John_Eric tracks. Stronger marketplace engagement and record purchase frequency could help revenue, where forecasts already point to 21% annual growth, but the benefit needs to come without further pressure on already thin profitability and on a balance sheet that carries a high level of debt.

Using 10.5% annual revenue growth and a future profit margin of 6.9%, the narrative from John_Eric estimates MercadoLibre's fair value at US$2,395 per share. This reflects a view that current reinvestment in logistics and credit eventually supports that level of normalized profitability.

title: MercadoLibre vs. Target: Which Stock Looks More Compelling Now?
detail:
MercadoLibre vs. Target: Which Stock Looks More Compelling Now?
Vrishali Bagree
Tue, November 24, 2026 at 8:32 AM EST 6 min read
MELI
TGT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI and Target Corporation TGT are pursuing strategic initiatives to strengthen customer engagement, expand revenue opportunities and build sustainable earnings power. Their latest quarterly results offer insights into the effectiveness of these investments and their potential to generate long-term shareholder value.

MercadoLibre is a leading e-commerce and financial technology company in Latin America, operating across online marketplaces, digital payments, lending, logistics and advertising. MELI is benefiting from the increasing adoption of online shopping and digital financial services. Target, a prominent U.S. general merchandise retailer, is strengthening its business through differentiated merchandise, competitive pricing, store modernization, digital innovation and an enhanced shopping experience.

MercadoLibre and Target have market capitalizations of approximately $72.2 billion and $76.1 billion, respectively.

The Case for MELI

MercadoLibre continues to capitalize on the structural shift toward online commerce and digital financial services across Latin America. Its third-quarter 2026 net revenues and financial income increased 45% year over year, with market share gains across Brazil, Mexico and Argentina. Expanded free-shipping benefits, broader product selection and faster deliveries are encouraging repeat purchases and attracting customers. The company's expanding logistics infrastructure and investments in automation should enhance fulfillment efficiency, strengthen customer retention and support further marketplace penetration.

Mercado Pago remains a significant growth engine as consumers increasingly rely on the platform for everyday transactions, savings, investments and borrowing. Fintech monthly active users increased 29% year over year, while assets under management grew 67%. MercadoLibre's ability to leverage marketplace transaction data for credit underwriting and customer acquisition provides a competitive advantage. Improving credit card economics as existing customer cohorts mature, alongside stable delinquency trends, reinforces the fintech business's long-term earnings potential.

Advertising and artificial intelligence (AI) are creating additional avenues for monetization and operational efficiency. Advertising revenues increased 58% year over year in U.S. dollar terms, supported by improvements in AI-powered advertising tools and expanding retail media capabilities. The company's partnership with Netflix should extend its connected television advertising reach beginning in early 2027. Meanwhile, stronger engagement across commerce and fintech, expanding affiliate networks and declining per-shipment costs in Brazil provide a foundation for further market share gains and long-term profitability improvements.

Nonetheless, investments in free shipping, fulfillment capacity and affiliate marketing are weighing on near-term profitability. Third-quarter operating income declined 6% year over year, while the operating margin contracted 40 basis points sequentially to 6.3%. Rapid credit portfolio expansion also warrants monitoring amid challenging lending conditions in Brazil and Argentina despite disciplined underwriting practices and healthy asset quality.

Much of the squeeze looks like MercadoLibre's own choice, since rival Sea grew Shopee's profit despite its push into Brazil.

The risk that could last is credit: loans more than 90 days late are rising, and lenders like Nu Holdings trade at a fraction of MercadoLibre's multiple.

At 31x forward earnings, MercadoLibre trades near the low end of its five-year range, and the fourth-quarter report will test analysts' 44% EPS rebound for 2027.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) grew revenue 45% last quarter, yet its stock closed at $1,425.08 on Nov. 23, still about 7% below its Nov. 5 close of $1,530.28, the session after the report.

On Nov. 19, one investor made the case for buying the drop in a post shared on both r/stocks and r/ValueInvesting, titled: "$MELI is a gift at these prices."

The market disagrees, and two other stocks help explain why. Shopee, owned by Sea Limited (SE:NYSE), is the rival whose push into Brazil is a big reason MercadoLibre is spending so heavily on shipping. And Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE) lends to many of the same Brazilian and Mexican consumers that Mercado Pago's credit book is growing into.

The numbers check out

The 45% and the 6% come straight from MercadoLibre's third-quarter release on Nov. 4, which put revenue growth at 41% FX-neutral. MercadoLibre blamed the drop in operating income on more free shipping, new fulfillment capacity added ahead of the holiday peak, and more affiliate marketing spend in Brazil.

Consensus has 2026 EPS at $36.66, below 2025's $39.40, then $52.96 in 2027, a 44% jump. Analysts keep trimming that rebound, though: the 2027 estimate is about 6% lower than a month ago.

The margin squeeze is mostly a choice

MercadoLibre's operating margin has more than halved in under two years, from 13.5% in the fourth quarter of 2024 to 6.3% last quarter:

MercadoLibre (MELI): operating (EBIT) margin (%), last 8 quarters (to September 30, 2026) (TIKR)

The shipping spending is starting to pay off. In Brazil, cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency and sat 14% below its level in the first quarter of 2025.

Sea's results suggest the squeeze is mostly MercadoLibre's own doing. Sea CEO Forrest Li said Brazil remained Shopee's fastest-growing market in the third quarter, yet Shopee's adjusted EBITDA rose 45% to $269.2 million on 41% revenue growth. Nu Holdings NU is expanding its presence in Mexico, supported by growing customer adoption, its transition to a full-fledged bank and favorable digital banking trends. In the third quarter of 2026, the company's Mexican customer base increased 27% year over year to 16.6 million, representing 17% of the country's adult population. With 870,000 customer additions during the quarter, NU strengthened its position as Mexico's largest digital bank.

The transition to a bank marks an important milestone. Deposit insurance coverage increased sixteenfold, from approximately $12,000 to $195,000 per customer. Banking status also enables the company to offer payroll accounts, providing opportunities to capture salary deposits, deepen customer relationships and generate additional revenues through cross-selling financial products.

Nu Holdings is also focusing on improving its funding economics in Mexico. At the third quarter-end, deposits stood at $5.3 billion. The company is shifting toward lower-cost deposits while maintaining ample liquidity. Greater payroll account adoption could build a more stable and cost-effective funding base, supporting lending growth, net interest income and profitability.

Mexico's push toward digital payments presents another growth opportunity. On Oct. 20, 2026, the country's Congress approved legislation promoting digital payments and reducing reliance on cash. Greater digital adoption could provide richer transaction data, improve credit underwriting and expand lending opportunities.

Management sees substantial growth potential in Mexico, where credit card penetration remains at around 12%. Under its base-case scenario, the Mexican business could reach 70% of the scale of its Brazilian operations, while greater digitalization could enable it to match Brazil's scale. Nu Holdings' banking transition, expanding lending opportunities and greater scope for cross-selling financial products could help the company unlock additional revenue streams in Mexico.

How Do Itaú Unibanco & MercadoLibre Compete?

Itaú Unibanco ITUB competes with Nu Holdings through its extensive banking network, digital financial services and diversified product offerings, including credit cards, personal loans and investments. Its established presence across Brazil, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay strengthens its regional competitive positioning. As of Sept. 2026, ITUB has a presence in 18 countries and territories.

MercadoLibre MELI, through its fintech platform Mercado Pago, competes with Nu Holdings by offering digital payments, credit, savings and investment solutions across Latin America. Its established e-commerce ecosystem facilitates customer acquisition and cross-selling opportunities, particularly in Brazil, Mexico and Argentina. In the third quarter of 2026, Mercado Pago's monthly active users increased 29% year over year to 93 million.

Key Points

Interested in MercadoLibre, Inc.? Here are five stocks we like better.

The MSCI Emerging Markets Index has entered bear-market territory as semiconductor stocks, a stronger dollar, and political uncertainty weigh on valuations.

The iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF offers direct exposure to the index, while the Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF provides broader diversification at a lower cost.

MercadoLibre, Nu Holdings, and dLocal have fallen sharply despite reporting strong revenue growth or record profits.

The global sell-off in AI and technology stocks has left its mark on the developing world. On Friday, Nov. 20, the MSCI Emerging Markets Index fell for a seventh consecutive session and officially entered bear market territory, now more than 20% below its June peak. It was also the index's worst week since March 2020.

That decline has pushed emerging-market valuations to levels that are difficult to overlook. As of the close on Friday, Nov. 20, the index traded at a forward price-to-earnings ratio (P/E) last seen during the crisis of 2008, well below every other major region. Market participants now have to weigh whether this marks a generational buying opportunity, or whether emerging markets are cheap for good reason, such as forward earnings no longer being as visible or likely as they previously were.

→ Zscaler Got a Boost From Palo Alto, But Now It Has to Deliver

What Triggered the Selling

The pressure has come from several directions at once, and each has compounded the others.

The unwinding of the AI trade has been the biggest single driver. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (NYSE: TSM), Samsung Electronics (OTCMKTS: SSNLF), and SK hynix (NASDAQ: SKHY) together make up close to 28% of the MSCI Emerging Markets Index, so a sell-off in chip stocks hits emerging markets harder than almost anywhere else. Taiwan's stock market fell 17.5% in the week to Nov. 20, its worst five-day stretch since 1990.

→ Keysight Technologies: The Tollbooth on the Technology Superhighway

A surging U.S. dollar has added to the strain. The U.S. Dollar Index reached 103.97 on Nov. 19, its highest level since April 2025, before closing at 103.81 on Nov. 20. A stronger dollar tends to weigh on emerging markets by pulling capital back toward the U.S., raising the cost of dollar-denominated debt and eroding the value of local-currency returns for U.S.-based investors.

Interest rate expectations are closely tied to that move. Hotter-than-expected inflation readings have pushed markets to price in a high probability of another Federal Reserve rate hike in December 2026. That has kept U.S. yields elevated and made the higher-risk returns of emerging markets less attractive by comparison.
